extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models
extraction.description: A dataset of 506 human-crafted image-instruction-response samples for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models across eight visual scenarios.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 235, 2024)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from LAION-5B using keyword search with CLIP-retrieval for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories; from the Rico dataset for Application Usage; from Open WebText Initiative website links for Web Usage screenshots; and from test sets of existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA, STVQA, ESTVQA) which were reannotated with novel instruction-response pairs. Images were manually filtered for some categories and heuristically filtered with PaddleOCR for others. Human authors wrote instructions and reference responses, and MTurk workers verified sample correctness.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LAION-5B images, Rico dataset UI screens, Open WebText Initiative website screenshots, and images from InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA test sets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images from existing datasets were reannotated with new instruction-response pairs; some categories were manually filtered, while others were filtered using OCR-based heuristics and selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of detected words.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual filtering for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories; heuristic filtering using PaddleOCR for Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes; selection of top 500 OCR-rich images; verification by MTurk workers and cross-review by author groups; incorrect samples were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human authors created instruction-response pairs following annotation guidelines. MTurk workers verified each sample's correctness. For human performance baseline, selected annotators wrote responses to all instruction-image pairs. For human evaluation, three MTurk annotators independently judged whether predicted responses were acceptable given the image, instruction, and reference response, with majority vote used as the final decision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human evaluation, each predicted response was judged independently by three annotators and the final label was determined by majority vote. The paper reports 96% of Stage 2 samples were annotated correctly after verification and filtering. Human evaluation acceptance ratings were computed from majority vote.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 for human evaluation judgments; 1 reference response per dataset item
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators were mainly from the US.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4), CLIP-retrieval UI, GPT-4, GPT-4V, BLEURT, Rouge-L, BERTScore
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples is released as a validation set with reference responses, while 406 samples are kept hidden. The paper states that the dataset and code are available on the project page and that a continuously updated leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was observed; the paper states that images, instructions, and reference responses were intended to avoid offensive content. Annotators were mainly from the US.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to benchmark context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in multimodal models, with potential relevance to assisting visually impaired users and other real-world applications. The paper discusses possible harmful model outputs and the need for diverse annotator regions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that human responses and evaluation may vary across social groups and that annotators were mainly from the US, which may affect linguistic diversity and writing style. It also notes that models may be biased by prior visual knowledge and training data diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging for current multimodal models, especially on time reading, infographics, and fine-grained perception tasks. Human evaluation is expensive and time-consuming. The paper notes that few-shot examples do not substantially improve context-sensitive reasoning and that synthetic generation remains difficult.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation/benchmarking of large multimodal models; zero-shot and few-shot testing; human baseline comparison; automatic and human evaluation of model responses; validation set for model development.
